content.value_statement: Python teams need consistent tests that cover behavior without slowing delivery. This skill provides practical pytest patterns for fixtures, mocking, async code, coverage, and CI.
actual_capabilities: Explains unit, integration, functional, and performance test roles.
Shows pytest tests using arrange, act, and assert structure.
Demonstrates fixtures, parameterization, monkeypatching, and temporary files.
Covers mocking for API clients and external dependencies.
Includes async testing, database testing, coverage reporting, and CI examples.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not an executable test runner.
Examples use placeholder services, local databases, and sample application names.
It does not customize tests for a project without seeing that project code.
It does not replace security review for integration tests that touch real services.

use_cases.title: Create a first pytest suite
use_cases.description: Turn core Python functions into clear tests with setup, action, and assertion steps.

use_cases.title: Improve service test isolation
use_cases.description: Mock API calls, environment variables, files, and database state so tests stay repeatable.

use_cases.title: Standardize project testing
use_cases.description: Document fixtures, coverage settings, markers, and CI commands for a Python repository.

prompt_templates.title: Write basic tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to write pytest tests for this module. Include clear test names and arrange, act, assert structure.

prompt_templates.title: Add fixtures and parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Reduce repeated setup across related tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to refactor these tests with fixtures and parameterization. Keep each case readable and independent.

prompt_templates.title: Mock external dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Test code that calls services or reads configuration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to test this service without real network calls or real environment secrets. Use mocks and monkeypatching.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full test strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a mature repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to propose a test strategy for this repository. Cover fixtures, async tests, database tests, coverage, and CI.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for tests for a calculator module.
output_examples.output: The skill produces concise pytest cases for normal inputs, edge cases, and expected errors, with descriptive names.

output_examples.input: A backend service calls an external API during tests.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends mocks for the HTTP calls and assertions that verify request behavior without reaching the network.

output_examples.input: A team wants coverage in continuous integration.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines coverage commands, reporting options, markers, and workflow steps suitable for a Python project.

best_practices: Keep tests independent and clean up shared state after each run.
Use fixtures for repeated setup and parameterization for repeated cases.
Mock external systems unless the test is explicitly an integration test.
anti_patterns: Do not depend on real production services in routine unit tests.
Do not hide unclear behavior behind vague test names.
Do not chase coverage numbers without checking meaningful assertions.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It guides test design and provides examples that can be adapted to a project.

faq.question: Which test framework does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on pytest and related tools such as pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, and Hypothesis.

faq.question: Can it help with mocking APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to mock HTTP calls and verify behavior without real network requests.

faq.question: Does it cover database tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for in-memory databases, sessions, constraints, and fixture cleanup.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CI setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes coverage commands, pytest configuration, and a GitHub Actions example.

faq.question: Can it review my existing tests?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the tests and project context, then ask for gaps, duplication, and reliability issues.
